name: OpenSanctions
tagline: Supreme Data on Supreme Leaders — open international database of sanctions, PEPs, and entities of criminal or political interest
project_type: open data platform and compliance database
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
countries_deployed: Global (330+ data sources across multiple jurisdictions)
known_funders: German Federal Ministry for Education and Research (BMBF) — grant 01IS21S48, Sep 2021–Feb 2022
dependency_risks: dependence on government-published source data quality
scope limited by what governments publish officially

policy_outcomes.description: Data used in New York Times investigation exposing illicit flow of Western technology to Russia through Hong Kong shell companies
Data used to identify billionaires and oligarchs hiding assets and circumventing sanctions via financial firms in Cyprus

documented_limitations: coverage dependent on official government publications
PEP coverage varies significantly by country
matching API has known false positive risks at scale
non-commercial CC licence limits direct civil society reuse in commercial contexts
failure_modes: government source data removal or paywalling
false negatives in screening due to transliteration or alias gaps
legal challenges to inclusion of individuals
governance_model: for-profit GmbH (OpenSanctions Datenbanken GmbH) with founder-led management; open source codebase; data inclusion criteria published publicly
curation_criteria: Entities must appear on official sanctions lists, government watchlists, or meet documented criteria for PEP or criminal interest
contributor_governance: Community can submit data source suggestions and flag data issues; core pipeline maintained by paid team
community_ownership: Data: CC 4.0 Attribution NonCommercial; Code: MIT licence
controversies: Individuals have requested removal from database; deletion policy published but contested
Inclusion of Russian company data from 2022 prompted questions about data completeness and political framing
political_bias_allegations: None formal; database reflects official government sanctions designations which may themselves carry geopolitical bias
legal_regulatory_issues: GDPR-relevant data on individuals; privacy policy and deletion request process published; operates under German law

government_partnerships.name: GLEIF (Global LEI Foundation)
government_partnerships.role: collaboration to enhance sanctions and AML screening using Legal Entity Identifiers

ai_involvement: LLM-assisted text extraction used for entity data ingestion from unstructured sources, with human moderation; matching API uses ML-based scoring for entity resolution
